items.stem: An application will move to the cloud with minimal changes, just re-hosting the VMs. Which of the 7 Rs is this?

options.rationale: Correct: rehosting moves workloads with minimal change.
Repurchase replaces the app with a SaaS product.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound practices when planning migration waves? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Sequence waves so dependencies migrate before dependents
options.rationale: Correct: dependencies must move first to avoid breaking apps.

options.text: Start with lower-risk applications to build momentum and learning
options.rationale: Correct: early low-risk waves reduce risk and build capability.

options.text: Migrate every application simultaneously with no sequencing
options.rationale: A big-bang move raises risk and ignores dependencies.

options.text: Skip the portfolio assessment to save time
options.rationale: Skipping assessment leads to poor strategy choices.

items.explanation: Correct: Sequence waves so dependencies migrate before dependents, Start with lower-risk applications to build momentum and learning.

items.stem: Why build a business case and TCO comparison before migrating?

options.text: To justify the investment and choose the right strategy per application
options.rationale: Correct: the business case and TCO guide investment and strategy decisions.

options.text: Because AWS refuses migrations without one
options.rationale: It is good practice, not an AWS gate.

options.text: To permanently lock the architecture with no changes
options.rationale: A business case does not lock architecture.

options.text: To avoid ever needing validation at cutover
options.rationale: Validation is still required at cutover regardless.

items.explanation: Correct: To justify the investment and choose the right strategy per application.
